contracts.title: EcoFuturesAdmin -- who is who
contracts.notice: Identity and standing for every actor, and the protocol directory. It holds no money. Trust Admins (Holders) admitted, removed and replaced only by Council vote, through Governance Verifiers admitted by a Holder of their own country, in organisations bound to ONE Holder Standing suspension and dismissal of verifiers; the freeze of a Holder (Governance) Identity the automated identity check (the server marks it): one record per person links all of that person's wallets. GTAs, Holders and verifiers pass it before they are admitted; a patron passes it to buy (FM p2) Organisations the unit of independence: a person belongs to one at a time. A verifier who moves gets a new wallet in the new organisation; the old one keeps its seats but takes no new work, and the person never challenges, attests, claims or is reseated on its former organisation's covenants. A country needs two organisations before its first verification (FM p6) Agreements the digital agreements each party accepted, by hash

Nothing is migrated: the verifier keeps its admitting Holder, and holderOf() follows the line to whoever holds it now. Only a replaced Holder has a successor, so the line is short and acyclic by construction.

contracts.name: EcoCountries
contracts.title: EcoCountries -- the rulebook: countries, their settings, and the flows they follow
contracts.notice: What a request in each country must go through and what it costs. NOT DEPLOYED ON ITS OWN (merged copy, 19 Oct 2026). EcoEditions inherits this rulebook: one contract, at one address, which the directory names twice (`countries` and `editions`), so every caller and every gate is unchanged. The views only the portal reads -- the fee quote, the price floor for a listing, the term range, a decoded flow -- are EcoLens's, rebuilt from `getCountry`, `defaultBaseFee` and `flowCode`. THE FLOW, per country, as data: an ordered list of Steps, validated when it is defined. A country's five settings (Lifecycle v5 §5) are a flow id (registration timing and the power), the term limits and the listing window, plus the window after a sale for path B's recording. For example: Sri Lanka, path A, under a power POWER, DEED, ATTEST, MINT, SALE Japan, path A DEED, ATTEST, MINT, SALE Brazil, path B AGREEMENT, MINT, SALE, RECORDING, ATTEST WHO CHANGES WHAT. The Foundation defines flows and enables a country with its first settings. After that a Trust Admin of the country proposes new settings, with the hash of counsel's note on the new law, and the Council decides by a majority of all seats (§5). A change applies only to requests made after it. Prices are not legal settings: a Trust Admin of the country, or a GTA, sets them directly.

contracts.name: EcoRegistry
contracts.title: EcoRegistry -- every request, from the guardian's payment to its covenant's activation
contracts.notice: THE FIXED HEAD, the same in every country (1 Oct 2026): requestVerification -> claim -> submitVerification -> watchdog window (challengeable) THEN THE COUNTRY'S FLOW (EcoCountries), one step at a time. EcoDeeds records each power, document and attestation and reports it here; the guardian mints; the Bank reports the sale. A covenant is active when its flow completes: at the sale in path A, at the recording's attestation in path B, which is why the price waits in the Bank's escrow between the two. THE MONEY HERE is the landowner's upfront payment (FM p9; TR3 Model B, 20 Oct, item 16), held per request in six fees and paid as each step is done. Each fee is zeroed when it is paid, and whatever is left when a request ends goes back to the landowner, so this contract's balance always equals the sum of what its requests still hold. verifierShare 1 verification, V x (1 + sqrt ha) -> the verifier at the first attestation, or when the landowner refuses to sign or abandons (flow B: at the mint) judgmentFee 2 judgment, D x (1.5 + sqrt ha) -> the watchdog-1 judges; otherwise the verifier when the watchdog window passes attestationFee 6 attestation, V -> the attester of the flow's last document Fees 3-5 -- the power's, the agreement's and the covenant's registration -- are the paper flow's: paid in here with the rest and passed to EcoDeeds, which holds them, pays each on proof of its step, and once the request has ended refunds what is left (EcoDeeds.refundFees; new money flows belong in EcoDeeds: this contract has no room). A request that ends any other way -- no claim, W1B upheld, the Deed not anchored, a failed attestation -- refunds the landowner what is left.

contracts.name: EcoDeeds
contracts.title: EcoDeeds -- the paper trail
contracts.notice: The digital mirror of every paper event in a covenant's flow (Lifecycle v5 §2): each document's hash, date and registration number, and the independent attester who confirms that the paper and its mirror match. The Registry holds the request, its money and its place in the flow; this contract records the evidence and tells the Registry when a step is done. power the Trust Admin grants the request's verifier a power of attorney for this land, one land per power (1 Oct 2026), registers it, and records it from its own wallet once registered: the signed power, its end date, the registered copy and its registration number, in one call (20 Oct). The Holder then gives the verifier a true copy of the registered power for the Deed sitting document the verifier or the Trust Admin records the agreement, the deed or its recording; until it is attested it may be recorded again, to correct it attest one independent person confirms the document against the register, and the power where there is one. A test, not a challenge (1 Oct 2026). THE PAPER FEES (TR3 Model B, 20 Oct, item 16). Fees 3-5 come in with the landowner's upfront payment and wait here; each is paid only when its step is done, and whatever is unpaid goes back to the landowner once the request has ended (refundFees, permissionless: EcoRegistry has no room to call it at every end; measured 20 Oct): 3 the power's registration, P to the land's Holder, when it anchors the registered power 4 the agreement's registration, A to the verifier, when the agreement to grant is recorded 5 the covenant's registration, C0 + C1 ha to the verifier, when the registered Deed (path A) or the recorded grant (path B) is attested WHO ATTESTS (FM p12): a verifier of another organisation than the land's verifier, or a Trust Admin of the country other than the land's; from day 21 of the attestation clock, also a GTA. The attester uploads the registry's certified copy and folio extract and records the registration. THE CLOCKS (FM p4-5, p12-13), each from the moment its step became current: power 30 days for the Holder to record the registered power (20 Oct): shown only, nothing lapses; then the Council may move the land to another Holder anchoring 14 days to anchor the signed Deed (or agreement); extensions of 14 from the Holder and 14 from the Council. From day 7 the landowner or the Holder may anchor it. Not anchored in time: the request lapses and everything goes back to the landowner. The landowner's refusal to sign, recorded by the verifier, ends it too -- the verifier keeps its verification fee. attestation 30 days; extensions of 30 from the Holder and 30 from the Council. Not attested in time: the request lapses, everything back to the landowner. A corrected document restarts the clock. An extension is asked before the deadline, with its cause; the Holder decides the first within 3 days, and silence counts as granted; the second is the Council's; there is no third.

It completes the power step, starts the Deed's clock and pays the Holder fee 3.

contracts.name: EcoChallenge
contracts.title: EcoChallenge -- challenges, the review windows and the review pool
contracts.notice: THE MENU (Covenant Flow Map v25, p15-17). A challenger picks one option and lodges its evidence in the same transaction; the option alone decides what an upheld verdict does. watchdog 1 (the request, after its verification) W1A the verification is wrong upheld: the verifier is removed and flagged; the request goes back to unclaimed, the challenger with a 3-day first claim W1B the land cannot be covenanted upheld: the request ends and the landowner is refunded; the verifier is flagged the term (the covenant) T3A the Deed is not on the register blocked; the last attester loses its fee and is flagged; the Holder has 60 days to restore it, or the covenant closes early T3B the score is wrong the verifier loses the seat and is flagged; held until the new verifier re-verifies, then back-paid at the corrected score T3C natural damage a re-verification falls due within 14 days; no flag T3D a landowner breach blocked until the cure is re-verified; no flag T3E the block is wrong (the landowner) the block is lifted and the held amounts released; the verifier is flagged dismissed (any option): nothing changes; the challenger is flagged, unless it is the landowner a lapse or a withdrawal: no flag WHO RAISES: W1A-T3D, any verifier in standing of the country from another organisation than the land's verifier -- under the same Holder or not; T3E, only the landowner. One undecided challenge per subject at a time. T3A and T3B concern the verification and its review window, so they are raised inside an open window; T3C-T3E at any time in the term. WHO DECIDES: three judges drawn from the country's Trust Admins, excluding the covenant's own, the Trust Admins of both parties' organisations and any frozen one; GTAs fill the seats too few remain for. Two matching votes decide, upheld or dismissed. The clock: 7 days to answer, 7 for the verdict, one redraw of 7 -- 21 days from the raise; then it lapses, as dismissed, with no flag. THE REVIEW WINDOW: 30 days after each re-verification. An outside party attests it with the registry's new certified copy (a verifier of another organisation, a Trust Admin of the country other than the land's, or from day 21 a GTA): one act's fee at the close, and the unattested count resets. Three windows in a row unattested halt instalment releases until an attestation. THE REVIEW POOL is 1% of the sale, held here: one act's fee per scheduled window (the pool / the review acts). A decided term challenge is paid one act's fee: upheld 60% to the challenger and 40% to the judges, dismissed 40% to the judges; what is unpaid stays in the pool, and its remainder goes to the landowner after the End Date.

contracts.notice: The GTAs are the Council. Its decisions are made on chain: a GTA proposes an action, GTAs approve it, and it executes once a majority of ALL seats has approved (§3.1, §5). What the Council decides: ADD_GTA, REMOVE_GTA its own membership (the GTA being removed does not count) ADMIT_HOLDER Trust Admins (a Holder's replacement is a country vote: see below) FREEZE_HOLDER, UNFREEZE_HOLDER a Trust Admin's freeze; RATIFY_FREEZE keeps an emergency freeze SET_COUNTRY_STATUS suspending or resuming a country REVOKE_POWER recording a power's revocation; an unauthorised one freezes the Holder SWITCH_PAYEE the payee when land changes hands or heirship is proven (§10) REASSIGN_VERIFIER moving a request to another of its Trust Admin's verifiers CLEAR_PARCEL releasing a parcel hash UNBLOCK_COVENANT, CANCEL_ the consequences a GTA reviews but never effects alone: unblocking, COVENANT, NOMINATE_VERIFIER, cancelling and reseating a covenant whose Trust Admin cannot act, the drip FREEZE_DRIP, SUSPEND_VERIFIER, valve, and a verifier's suspension or dismissal DISMISS_VERIFIER END_REWARD, EXTEND_CLOCK, fraud's end of TR3, a clock's second extension, a compulsory acquisition ACQUISITION CANCEL_ROOT cancelling an operation queued on the root's 7-day timelock (U3) RECORD_DOCUMENT the Articles, an authorisation, a certificate (G10) APPROVE_ROOT_OP the Council's key on an upgrade: the root schedules it only once approved (C5) COUNTRY VOTES -- the GTAs and the country's own Holders (not frozen), by more than half of them -- decide a Holder's replacement (FM p19, G3: it removes the Holder and names its Successor in the same country, whose fee and authority over every covenant follow at once), the country's fees (V, D and fees 3-5), and its module settings on a Holder's proposal with counsel's note (Ravi, 10 Oct: "based on GTA + TA (local only) vote"). The Foundation (the root) seats the first three GTAs -- below three seats no majority can act -- and changes the fee split through a 48-hour timelock. The emergency multisig (EMERGENCY_ROLE) may freeze a Trust Admin at once for 30 days; the Council ratifies it by day 30 or it lapses, and the multisig cannot use it on the same Trust Admin again for a year.

contracts.name: Tree
contracts.title: Tree -- TR3, the TREE reward
contracts.notice: An ERC-20 minted only by claims against what protected land has released. R's "TR3 -- the model in full" (320M, 22 Oct 2026), over the Covenant Flow Map v29 and the TR3 Model B FINAL note's stream (item 6). SUPPLY. 32 editions on the Fibonacci ladder, each issuing exactly 10,000,000 TR3 to land: 320,000,000 TR3, fixed. Where a land stands in them -- its place, the editions' OPEN, SETTLING and CLOSED states, promotion, the place fixed at listing, its sale -- is EcoEditions'. At the sale's completion this contract takes the land's allocation from there (its land-years at its edition's rate, at most 1,000,000 TR3) and starts its stream. Nothing is ever burned: every TR3 is minted, owed, streaming, unsold, committed to an overcharge or held by the Relics. THE STREAM, RELEASED FORWARD (C9). A covenant's allocation accrues evenly over its term. Each verification underwrites the interval after it: the stream runs at its score up to the HORIZON, the earlier of one interval after the verification and the next due date. At activation that is the verification before the sale plus one interval, never past the first due date. TR3 is claimable as it accrues. At each settlement the score's shortfall -- span x (100 - score) / 100 -- drops to the Relics. The split never changes: patron (the EFT's owner) 90%, landowner 10% of which the referrer takes 30%; a GTA referrer, or the land's own verifier, takes nothing (R4) and its share stays with the landowner. POINTS. Each settled span gives the land's Relic points: the TR3 released, plus the span's TR3 above the land's entry score (the score of the verification before the sale). EcoOvercharge shares every drop by points. CLAIMS (R, 14 Oct). The patron's share of what has streamed waits in the EFT's pool until the EFT's owner claims it; a sale passes the pool, and the rest of the stream, to the buyer, and nothing is minted at a transfer. Only the owner makes the patron claim. Anyone may trigger the guardian claim, which mints the landowner's and the referrer's shares and never touches the pool. A patron claim, a verification, an overcharge and an end void the EFT's open orders (EcoFuturesToken.voidOrders); the stream itself, and a guardian claim, do not. STOPS AND ENDS (Core, EcoParties and the Council report each): lateness the stream waits at the horizon -- not a hold. The verification, however late, releases the span held back at the score it records, and streams on (deferred, never forfeited) a stop a breach, Deed or partition block, or an upheld 3B: the stream stops at once. What accrues after is held: released by the verification that lifts it at its score, or, for a block lifted otherwise, up to the horizon at the score in force when it lifts; dropped to the Relics if the stream ends first. Money-only holds stop no TR3 an early end everything not yet streamed drops to the Relics; capacity never reopens; the land's Relic shatters the End Date closeTerm, after the final verification; anything still held drops to the Relics, and the land's Relic wakes -- or shatters, if a breach, Deed or partition hold stands AN OVERCHARGE (EcoOvercharge). An awake Relic commits TR3 from its balance: at most M x the allocation not yet streamed, within 1,000,000 TR3 a land in all. Each commitment keeps its ratio q = commit / allocation not yet streamed; each settled span then pays span x q x score of it with the land's stream, and what the score holds back carries back to that Relic. Whatever a commitment has not paid when the stream ends, or the share of it an acquisition takes, carries back too. At most MAX_BOOSTS commitments a land. An overcharge never uses edition capacity.

contracts.name: EcoOvercharge
contracts.title: EcoOvercharge -- the Relics: their points, their shared TR3, the overcharge, and forging
contracts.notice: R's "TR3 -- the model in full" (320M, 22 Oct 2026): the Relics are funded by everything land does not earn. They have no issuance of their own; their TR3 is part of the 320,000,000. BIRTH. Every covenant's Relic is born at its activation, in its edition, and travels with the EFT while it CHARGES. POINTS. A Relic's points are the TR3 its land releases, plus the TR3 it releases above its entry score (the score of the verification before the sale): so restoring land makes a stronger Relic, and clearing it first gains nothing. Tree reports them as each span settles. Boosts paid to the land are not its points. DROPS. Everything land does not earn drops to the Relics -- the score's shortfall, the rest of a covenant that ends early, an edition's free room at its close, a land's TR3 above the 1,000,000 cap, a shattered Relic's balance -- and is shared among every Relic, charging or awake, in proportion to its points (an accumulator: each Relic's share is its points x the TR3 per point dropped since it last changed, rounded down, so the Relics never hold more than was dropped). A drop that finds no points, and the accumulator's rounding, wait for the next. WAKING AND SHATTERING. At a completed End Date the Relic wakes: it is minted as its own token to the EFT's owner, its balance becomes spendable, and it keeps its points and its share of drops. On an early end, or a breach, Deed or partition hold standing at the End Date, it shatters: its balance drops to all Relics and its points lapse. An acquired part shatters that share of it. THE OVERCHARGE. An awake Relic commits TR3 from its balance to land still streaming that the caller owns: up to M x the land's allocation not yet streamed, M = max(1, sqrt(reward at the Relic's edition / reward at the land's)), and within 1,000,000 TR3 per land, its own allocation and every commitment included. Tree pays it with the land's stream, at the land's score; what the land does not mint of it -- the score's shortfall, or the rest when the land ends -- carries back to the Relic that committed it, to apply again. Several Relics may back one land. FORGING. Two awake Relics of one edition (2 or later) forge into one of the edition before: their points and their balances add. Relics are never burned.

contracts.name: EcoEditions
contracts.title: EcoEditions -- the editions and the places in them, and the country rulebook (EcoCountries)
contracts.notice: MERGED (merged copy, 19 Oct 2026): this contract also carries EcoCountries, which it inherits; the directory names this one address twice, `countries` and `editions`, so every caller and every gate is unchanged. The views only the portal reads (an edition's view and state, the current edition, the estimate, the unallocated TR3, the programme's capacity, the land limits, the ladder) are EcoLens's, rebuilt from `rawEdition`. Where every land stands in the editions, from its watchdog's close to its sale. R's "TR3 -- the model in full" (320M, 22 Oct 2026) over the TR3 Model B build note, FINAL, item 10 ("Editions close only when full"); Tree keeps the streams. EDITIONS. 32 editions, each issuing exactly 10,000,000 TR3 to land: 320,000,000 in all. Edition k holds SCALE x F(min(k, 10)) x F(k) land-years (1,000 x F(min(k, 10)) x F(k) hectare-years in production), so it pays 10,000 / (F(min(k, 10)) x F(k)) TR3 a hectare-year at a score of 100: the genesis squares to Edition 9, then each edition divides the reward by 1.618. A title may take at most 100 x F(k) hectare-years (10,000 x F(k) land-years; 33.33 x F(k) hectares at the 3-year minimum). PLACING. A sign-up holds no room: it takes its parcel, and its land must fit the open edition's limits. The Registry queues the land when its verification is filed; it takes its place when its watchdog window closes with no challenge undecided, in the order the windows close (placeDue, run by every call that needs it and by anyone). It is placed whole in the OPEN edition; a land that does not fit the room left sends the edition to SETTLING and goes whole into the next, which opens one step down. NO CLOCK. An edition closes only when land fills it: it stays OPEN at its reward however long that takes. A SETTLING edition finally closes when every place in it has activated; until then room released in it goes to the next land that fits and whose EFT has not been listed (promote: a land moves up, and is allocated again at the earlier edition's reward). At the final close its room still free drops to the Relics. A land's reward is fixed once its EFT is listed: a listed land never moves. FINALITY. When Edition 32 is full no land enters again: sign-ups are refused, and a land still waiting for a place cannot be listed (its request ends as any unsold request does). Covenants stream on to their End Dates. SOLD. At the sale's completion Tree sells the place: S grows, and the allocation is its land-years at its edition's rate, capped at 1,000,000 TR3; Tree drops the excess to the Relics.

Merged copy (19 Oct 2026): the rulebook (EcoCountries) and the editions are one contract, and the views only the portal reads are here, under their old names, rebuilt from that contract's raw state.

functions.name: capacityOf
functions.notice: An edition's capacity in land-years: SCALE x F(min(k, 10)) x F(k).

functions.name: currentEdition
functions.notice: The OPEN edition now; 0 once Edition 32 is full (no clock since item 10).

functions.name: editions
functions.notice: Every edition as it stands now: several can be OPEN or SETTLING at once (R, 13 Oct, section 3).

functions.name: estimate
functions.notice: The edition a land of this size would be placed in now, and its TR3 over the term at this score (capped). Reverts once all are full, or when the land is over the open edition's limit.

functions.name: fees
functions.notice: What a request in this country, of this size, pays upfront (was EcoCountries.quote; TR3 Model B, 20 Oct, item 16): fee 1, the verification fee V x (1 + sqrt ha); fee 6, the attestation fee V; fee 2, the judgment fee D x (1.5 + sqrt ha); fee 3, P, only where the country's flow uses a power; fee 4, A, only where it has an agreement to grant; fee 5, C0 + C1 x ha.

functions.name: fib
functions.notice: The Fibonacci number: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ... 10,946 for the 21st, 2,178,309 for the 32nd.

functions.name: getFlow
functions.notice: A flow, decoded from the word each request keeps.

functions.name: limitOf
functions.notice: The most land-years one title may take in an edition: 100 x F(k) hectare-years.

functions.name: listingInfo
functions.notice: What a minted covenant's listing needs: whether its flow is at the sale, and by when the auction must complete (moved from EcoRegistry, 17 Oct, to make room there).

functions.name: maxLandUnits
functions.notice: The largest land the edition now open (or next) takes: 33.33 x F(k) hectares (at the shortest term).

functions.name: priceFloorFor
functions.notice: The price floor a new request of this size and term would be held to, at today's fees (item 9).

functions.name: programmeCapacity
functions.notice: The land-years the 32 editions hold.

functions.name: rewardOf
functions.notice: TR3 (wei) a hectare-year at a score of 100: 10,000 / (F(min(k, 10)) x F(k)).

functions.name: stepOf
functions.notice: An edition's step: its number, up to 32 (TR3 Model B item 10).

functions.name: termRange
functions.notice: The terms land of this size may take in this country now: the country's limits within what the current edition allows the land. minYears > maxYears means none.

functions.name: unallocatedTR3
functions.notice: The TR3 of the editions' room not yet sold: the room of editions not finally closed (their places included). Tree's `unallocated` matches it to within rounding dust.

functions.name: wouldReserve
functions.notice: The edition a land of this size would be placed in now, or 0 once all are full: the OPEN one, or the next when it does not fit the room left (an estimate: lands queued before it may take the room first).

contracts.name: EcoLists
contracts.title: EcoLists -- the Lens's lists
contracts.notice: Paginated lists for the portal's queues and tables: requests, covenants, auctions, challenges, Relics, the resale market, the Council's proposals and country votes. Read-only, no state, redeployed with each release beside EcoLens (whose per-item screens it reuses for the market rows). It reads the directory from Admin. Every list scans ids downward from `cursor` (0 = the newest), at most `scan` of them, and returns the rows that match and `next`, the cursor for the following page (0 = nothing older). `scan` bounds one call's gas, measured cold (test/unit/Lists.t.sol, --isolate): about 115,000 a covenant or listing, 60,000 a request, 50,000 a challenge, 22,000 an auction -- so scan 100 covenants, 200 requests or challenges, 300 auctions, well inside an RPC's eth_call cap. In a filter, a zero value means "any". They replace V10.1's EcoLens.getAll... views and the portal's own capped scans; the backend's event index remains the place for search, sorting and history.

functions.name: auctions
functions.notice: The primary sale. `stage`: 0 any auction or settlement, 1 bidding open, 2 ended and not yet settled, 3 settled and waiting for the winner's identity check.

functions.name: challenges
functions.notice: Challenges: the queues (undecided, by country), a judge's (judge), a request's or a covenant's history (kind and subject), a party's (party).

functions.name: countryVotes
functions.notice: Country votes, open only or all, in one country or every (country zero).

functions.name: covenants
functions.notice: Covenants: a verifier's re-verification queue (verifier, dueBy), seats to refill (vacantSeat), a landowner's lands, a patron's portfolio (owner), the overcharged (boosted), the ended (status ENDED).

functions.name: listings
functions.notice: The resale market: EFTs with a live listing, or (withOffers) a live listing or a live offer.

functions.name: proposals
functions.notice: The Council's proposals, open only or all.

functions.name: relics
functions.notice: Relics, a wallet's or all (owner zero): awake Relics are their own tokens; a charging Relic travels with its EFT. Shattered and forged Relics are left out.

functions.name: requests
functions.notice: Requests: the claim queue (OPEN, a country), the unclaimed for assignment (OPEN, old), a landowner's or a verifier's, those at a step (MINT, POWER, ATTEST ...), those in the watchdog (VERIFIED).

functions.name: verifierRecord
functions.notice: A verifier's record (TR3 Model B item 10's Lens line): the EcoScores it filed at verification -- their sum and number, so its mean is sum / number -- and how many of its scores review corrected: a W1A or a 3B upheld against it. Two windows, each as the lists page: requests from `cursor`, challenges from `chCursor`. Each land's threat data, its IUCN start and target bands, is in its request row.

roles.name: SERVER

roles.name: HOLDER
roles.doc: A country Trust Admin -- the Holder of the covenants its verifiers verify.

roles.name: GUARDIAN
roles.doc: A landowner. Granted by the protocol at its first mint; nobody admits a guardian.

roles.name: EMERGENCY
roles.doc: The Foundation's emergency multisig: the emergency freeze of a Holder and the emergency pause, both of which lapse after 30 days (FM p4, P5, P11). Held directly, not behind the root's timelock.
